Nolan Kido / Living Well

Sources & further reading

Primary sources

A small shelf with a clear purpose.

Looking for something to read, hear, or try? Browse the free-resource collection. This page explains sources behind specific article claims. The launch essays are principally original editorial arguments. The sources below support specific risk and oral-history guidance. They do not establish that the optional practices improve wellbeing or prove any spiritual interpretation. Links were checked during the October 8, 2026 build.

NIST: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile

Read the publication page or the report (PDF). The 2024 profile discusses confabulation, data privacy, and human-AI configuration among its risk areas. It informs the cautions about verification and dependence in AI-generated reflections and values before advice. It is a risk-management document, not a study validating the exercises on this website.

Oral History Association: ethics and best practices

Read the ethics statement and best-practice guidance. These support the emphasis on informed participation, agreed use, narrator review, and preservation in the family-story guide. The website's worksheet is an editorial planning aid, not the association's form or a legal release.

Library of Congress: preserving family stories

Read Preserving Family Stories. This introduction offers a way into oral-history collections and family interviewing. Use it to broaden your questions, not to assume that any person owes you a recorded story.

Two related places on this website

A working tool versus a trustworthy one examines independent checks. The decision-record worksheet helps preserve what was known at the time of a decision. The Technology section focuses on tools; Living Well asks what those tools are for.

How this shelf will grow

Add sources when a real article needs them. Prefer the original work, identify translations or adaptations, and explain disagreements. A long link list is not a substitute for reading carefully. Broken links and misattributions can be reported through contact.
